articles.title: Outside Directors' Departures
articles.topic: 外部董事的突然离职：信号与代价
articles.source: 2011 年考研英语（二）Text 1 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs's board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University.
sentences.cn: 2000 年 1 月，鲁思·西蒙斯以外部董事的身份加入高盛董事会；一年后，她出任布朗大学校长。

sentences.en: For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism.
sentences.cn: 在那个十年余下的时间里，她显然同时胜任这两个角色，没有招致多少批评。

sentences.en: But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked?
sentences.cn: 但到 2009 年底，西蒙斯女士因曾在高盛薪酬委员会任职而备受抨击——她怎么能让那些巨额奖金的发放悄然过关呢？

sentences.en: By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board.
sentences.cn: 到第二年 2 月，西蒙斯已经离开了董事会。

sentences.en: The position was just taking up too much time, she said.
sentences.cn: 她说，这个职位实在占用了太多时间。

sentences.en: Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board.
sentences.cn: 外部董事理应在公司董事会中充当有益而又较少偏见的顾问。

sentences.en: Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals.
sentences.cn: 由于财富和名望都是在别处挣得的，他们想必拥有足够的独立性，能够对首席执行官的提案提出异议。

sentences.en: If the sky, and the share price is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.
sentences.cn: 如果天要塌下来、股价不断下跌，外部董事应当能凭借自己曾经渡过危机的经验提出建议。

sentences.en: The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004.
sentences.cn: 俄亥俄大学的研究者使用了一个数据库，它涵盖 1989 至 2004 年间的一万多家公司和六万四千多名不同的董事。

sentences.en: Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next.
sentences.cn: 然后，他们只是查看哪些董事从一份委托声明书留任到了下一份。

sentences.en: The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70.
sentences.cn: 离开董事会最可能的原因是年龄，因此研究者把注意力集中在 70 岁以下董事的那些“意外”离任上。

sentences.en: They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%.
sentences.cn: 他们发现，在一次意外离职之后，公司随后不得不重报盈利的概率会增加近 20%。

words.meaning: 词组：重报盈利（更正财报）

sentences.en: The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse.
sentences.cn: 被列入联邦集体诉讼被告名单的可能性也会上升，公司股票的表现还可能变得更糟。

sentences.en: The effect tended to be larger for larger firms.
sentences.cn: 公司规模越大，这种效应往往越明显。

sentences.en: Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship.
sentences.cn: 虽然他们的离开与公司随后的糟糕表现之间的相关性耐人寻味，但这并不意味着这些董事总是在弃沉船而逃。

words.meaning: adj. 引人联想的，耐人寻味的

sentences.en: Often they "trade up," leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.
sentences.cn: 他们常常是在“向上流动”：离开风险较高的小公司，转投规模更大、更稳定的公司。

words.meaning: 词组：向上升级，越换越好

sentences.en: But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred.
sentences.cn: 但研究者认为，如果外部董事在坏消息传出之前离开公司，就更容易避免声誉受损——即便回顾历史可以发现，不当行为发生时他们就在董事会任职。

sentences.en: Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.
sentences.cn: 想让外部董事陪伴自己渡过艰难时期的公司，可能不得不设置激励措施。

sentences.en: Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
sentences.cn: 否则，外部董事们就会效仿西蒙斯女士——她如今在校园里再度广受欢迎。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Ms. Simmons was criticized for ______.
questions.stem_cn: 根据第一段，西蒙斯女士受到批评是因为______。

options.C: refusing to make compromises
options.D: leaving the board in tough times

options_cn.C: 拒绝做出妥协
options_cn.D: 在困难时期离开董事会

questions.explanation: 定位第一段③句：她因曾在高盛薪酬委员会任职而备受抨击——“她怎能让那些巨额奖金发放悄然过关？”即人们认为她身为薪酬委员会成员未尽到监督职责，B 正确。A 无据（受抨击非因牟利）；C 无据；D 因果颠倒，她是先被批评后才离开董事会。

questions.stem: We learn from Paragraph 2 that outside directors are supposed to be ______.
questions.stem_cn: 由第二段可知，外部董事理应是______。

options.C: share price forecasters

options_cn.C: 股价预测者
options_cn.D: 独立的顾问

questions.explanation: 定位第二段①②句：外部董事应是“有益而少偏见的顾问”，且拥有“足够的独立性”去质疑首席执行官的提案，综合即“独立的顾问”，D 正确。B 偷换身份——他们是顾问（advisers）而非高管（executives）；A、C 均无文中依据。

questions.stem: According to the researchers from Ohio University, after an outside director's surprise departure, the firm is likely to ______.
questions.stem_cn: 根据俄亥俄大学的研究者，外部董事意外离职后，公司很可能______。

options.C: do less well in the stock market

options_cn.C: 在股市上表现较差
options_cn.D: 在诉讼中表现更糟

questions.explanation: 定位第三段④⑤句：意外离职后，公司被迫重报盈利的概率增加近 20%，涉联邦集体诉讼的可能性上升，且“股票的表现可能更糟”，C 正确。A 与文意相反；B 曲解 restate earnings（重报、更正盈利，并非盈利增加）；D 偷换——是“涉诉概率上升”而非“在诉讼中表现更糟”。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that outside directors ______.
questions.stem_cn: 由最后一段可以推断，外部董事______。

options.A: may stay for the attractive offers from the firm
options.B: have often had records of wrongdoings in the firm
options.C: are accustomed to stress-free work in the firm
options.D: will decline incentives from the firm

options_cn.A: 可能因公司开出的诱人条件而留下
options_cn.B: 常常在公司里有不当行为的记录
options_cn.C: 习惯了公司里没有压力的工作
options_cn.D: 会拒绝公司提供的激励

questions.explanation: 定位末段②③句：想在困难时期留住外部董事的公司“可能不得不设置激励措施”，否则他们就会像西蒙斯一样离开。言外之意：若有诱人的条件，外部董事可能留下来，A 正确（attractive offers 对应原文 incentives）。D 与此相反；B 曲解①句（在职期间发生过不当行为≠他们有不当行为记录）；C 无据。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the role of outside directors is ______.
questions.stem_cn: 作者对外部董事作用的态度是______。

options.C: scornful

options_cn.C: 轻蔑的
options_cn.D: 批评的

questions.explanation: 态度题。第二段以“有益而少偏见的顾问”“有足够独立性”“能凭渡过危机的经验提建议”正面刻画外部董事的作用；三、四段虽指出其突然离职的负面信号，但也说明这并非总是“弃船而逃”，并建议公司设法留住他们。可见作者总体上肯定外部董事的价值，B 正确。

articles.title: American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival
articles.topic: 报纸之死？——美国报业的危机求生
articles.source: 2011 年考研英语（二）Text 2 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers?
sentences.cn: 报纸的“死亡”后来到底怎么样了？

sentences.en: A year ago the end seemed near.
sentences.cn: 一年前，末日似乎已近在眼前。

sentences.en: The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet.
sentences.cn: 经济衰退眼看要夺走尚未流向互联网的那部分广告和读者。

sentences.en: Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom.
sentences.cn: 像《旧金山纪事报》这样的报纸正在记录自己的末日。

sentences.en: America's Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers.
sentences.cn: 美国联邦贸易委员会发起了一轮关于如何拯救报纸的讨论。

sentences.en: Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them?
sentences.cn: 报纸应该变成慈善机构吗？政府应该补贴它们吗？

sentences.en: It will hold another meeting soon.
sentences.cn: 它很快还将举行另一场会议。

sentences.en: But the discussions now seem out of date.
sentences.cn: 但这些讨论现在看来已经过时了。

sentences.en: In much of the world there is little sign of crisis.
sentences.cn: 在世界上许多地方，几乎看不到危机的迹象。

sentences.en: German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession.
sentences.cn: 德国和巴西的报纸已把经济衰退轻松甩在了身后。

sentences.en: Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit.
sentences.cn: 即便是身处全球报业最困难角落的美国报纸，也不仅存活了下来，而且常常重新实现了盈利。

sentences.en: Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same.
sentences.cn: 虽不是几年前司空见惯的 20% 利润率，但毕竟还是盈利。

sentences.en: It has not been much fun.
sentences.cn: 这个过程并不轻松愉快。

sentences.en: Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard.
sentences.cn: 许多报纸靠着把记者“抛下船”（裁员），才得以维持不沉。

words.meaning: 词组：维持不倒闭，免于破产
词组：把记者抛下船（喻裁员）

sentences.en: The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007.
sentences.cn: 美国新闻编辑协会估计，自 2007 年以来已有 13500 个新闻编辑部职位消失。

sentences.en: Readers are paying more for slimmer products.
sentences.cn: 读者花更多的钱，买到的却是更“瘦身”的报纸。

sentences.en: Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs.
sentences.cn: 一些报纸甚至大着胆子拒绝向偏远郊区送报。

sentences.en: Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further.
sentences.cn: 然而事实证明，这些孤注一掷的措施是正确的；而且对许多记者来说很不幸，这些措施还可以推行得更远。

sentences.en: Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers.
sentences.cn: 报纸正在成为更均衡的企业：来自读者与广告商的收入构成更加健康。

sentences.en: American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads.
sentences.cn: 美国报纸对广告的依赖，长期以来都极不寻常。

sentences.en: Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD).
sentences.cn: 据经济合作与发展组织（OECD）统计，2008 年美国报纸整整 87% 的收入来自广告。

sentences.en: In Japan the proportion is 35%.
sentences.cn: 在日本，这一比例是 35%。

sentences.en: Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.
sentences.cn: 毫不奇怪，日本报纸要稳定得多。

words.meaning: 词组：不出所料，毫不奇怪

sentences.en: The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive.
sentences.cn: 席卷新闻编辑部的这场旋风伤害了所有人，但大部分损害集中在报纸最缺乏特色的领域。

words.meaning: adj. 有特色的，与众不同的

sentences.en: Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters.
sentences.cn: 汽车和电影评论员走了，科学记者和一般财经记者也走了。

sentences.en: Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off.
sentences.cn: 驻外办事处被无情地砍掉。

sentences.en: Newspapers are less complete as a result.
sentences.cn: 结果，报纸变得不那么齐全完整了。

sentences.en: But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.
sentences.cn: 但在报纸行业，完整性已不再是一种优点。

questions.stem: By saying "Newspapers like ... their own doom" (Lines 3-4, Para. 1), the author indicates that newspapers ______.
questions.stem_cn: 作者说“像……的报纸正在记录自己的末日”（第一段 3-4 行），意在表明报纸______。

options.C: were not charitable corporations

options_cn.C: 不是慈善机构
options_cn.D: 处境绝望

questions.explanation: 例证反推题。划线句前后：一年前“末日似乎已近”、衰退“威胁夺走广告和读者”、政府发起“拯救报纸”的讨论，划线句以《旧金山纪事报》为例印证报纸当时命悬一线的处境，D 正确。A 相反（报纸清楚记录着危机）；B、C 利用后文“慈善机构”“政府补贴”的讨论设障，均非划线句要说明的内容。

questions.stem: Some newspapers refused delivery to distant suburbs probably because ______.
questions.stem_cn: 一些报纸拒绝向偏远郊区送报，可能是因为______。

options.C: journalists reported little about these areas

options_cn.C: 记者很少报道这些地区
options_cn.D: 订户抱怨报纸越来越薄

questions.explanation: 定位第三段⑤句。题干问“可能的原因”，需联系上下文推测：本段②句报社裁员求生、④句读者花更多钱买更薄的报纸、⑤句拒送偏远郊区，这些都是报社为渡过危机而压缩开支的措施，故拒送远郊的动机是降低成本，B 正确。A、C、D 均无文中依据。

questions.stem: Compared with their American counterparts, Japanese newspapers are much more stable because they ______.
questions.stem_cn: 与美国同行相比，日本报纸稳定得多，是因为它们______。

options.C: are less dependent on advertising

options_cn.C: 对广告的依赖更小
options_cn.D: 受读者数量的影响更小

questions.explanation: 定位第四段：美国报纸 87% 的收入来自广告，而日本只有 35%，紧接着总结“毫不奇怪，日本报纸稳定得多”——可推知其稳定的原因正是对广告依赖小，C 正确。A 偷换概念（是收入构成比例更健康，而非来源更多）；B 曲解 balanced businesses；D 无据。

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about the current newspaper business?
questions.stem_cn: 关于当前的报纸行业，由末段可以推断出什么？

options.A: Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.
options.B: Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspapers.
options.C: Foreign bureaus play a crucial role in the newspaper business.
options.D: Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews.

options_cn.A: 特色是报纸至关重要的特质
options_cn.B: 完整性是报纸失败的罪魁祸首
options_cn.C: 驻外办事处在报业中发挥关键作用
options_cn.D: 读者对汽车和电影评论失去了兴趣

questions.explanation: 定位末段：损害集中于报纸“最缺乏特色”的领域，无特色板块纷纷被砍，而“完整性已不再是报纸行业的优点”——反向推知：报纸要生存，靠的不是求全，而是特色，A 正确。B 过度推断（“不再是优点”≠“是失败的罪魁”）；C 与“驻外办事处被无情砍掉”相悖；D 过度推断，板块消失是因不具特色，而非读者失去兴趣。

questions.stem: The most appropriate title for this text would be ______.
questions.stem_cn: 本文最合适的标题是______。

options.B: American Newspapers: Gone with the Wind
options.C: American Newspapers: A Thriving Business

options_cn.C: 美国报纸：一个生机勃勃的行业
options_cn.D: 美国报纸：一个绝望的故事

questions.explanation: 主旨题。首段以“报纸之死怎么样了”设问并指出旧讨论已过时；第二段说美国报纸不仅存活还重新盈利；第三段写其裁员、减服务等求生措施；第四、五段写收入结构趋于均衡、砍掉无特色板块。全文主线是美国报业在危机中挣扎求生并逐步好转，A 切合主旨。B、D 与“起死回生”的基调相悖；C 言过其实。

articles.title: Less Is More: Postwar Housing
articles.topic: “少即是多”：战后美国的简约住宅风潮
articles.source: 2011 年考研英语（二）Text 3 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.
sentences.cn: 我们往往把二战后紧接着的几十年看作繁荣与增长的年代：数以百万计的士兵返回家园，依照《退伍军人权利法案》上大学，并在婚姻登记处排起长队。

sentences.en: But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more.
sentences.cn: 但说到他们的住宅，那却是一个讲求常识的年代——人们相信“少”确实可以是“多”。

sentences.en: During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.
sentences.cn: 在大萧条和战争期间，美国人学会了在物资匮乏中生活；这种克制，加上战后对未来的信心，使小而高效的住宅显得格外时尚。

sentences.en: Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living.
sentences.cn: 经济状况只是高效居住这一潮流的刺激因素之一。

sentences.en: The phrase "less is more" was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools.
sentences.cn: “少即是多”这句话实际上最早是由德国建筑师路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗推广开来的；和其他与包豪斯设计学院有关的人一样，他在二战前移居美国，并在美国的建筑院校任教。

sentences.en: These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.
sentences.cn: 这些设计师后来对美国建筑的发展进程产生了巨大影响，而其中影响最大的莫过于密斯。

sentences.en: Mies's signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot.
sentences.cn: 密斯这句招牌名言的意思是：安排得当的少量装饰，比大量装饰更有感染力。

sentences.en: Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance.
sentences.cn: 他认为，优雅并非源自繁多。

sentences.en: Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood – materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future.
sentences.cn: 和其他现代建筑师一样，他使用金属、玻璃和层压木材——这些材料今天我们习以为常，但在 20 世纪 40 年代却象征着未来。

sentences.en: Mies's sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.
sentences.cn: 密斯精妙的呈现方式掩盖了这样一个事实：他设计的空间小而高效，而非宽大却常常空旷。

sentences.en: The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller – two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet – than those in their older neighbors along the city's Gold Coast.
sentences.cn: 以密斯在芝加哥湖滨大道建造的典雅高楼为例，其中的公寓——不足 1000 平方英尺的两居室单元——比黄金海岸沿线那些较老的邻居楼里的公寓更小。

sentences.en: But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings' details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time.
sentences.cn: 但这些公寓大受欢迎：通透的玻璃墙、开阔的视野，以及建筑细节与比例的典雅——正是当时风行的抽象艺术在建筑上的对应物。

sentences.en: The trend toward "less" was not entirely foreign.
sentences.cn: “少”的潮流并非完全来自国外。

sentences.en: In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses – usually around 1,200 square feet – than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century.
sentences.cn: 20 世纪 30 年代，弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特开始建造比他在 19 世纪 90 年代和 20 世纪初设计的铺展式两层住宅更为质朴高效的房子——通常约 1200 平方英尺。

sentences.en: The "Case Study Houses" commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the "less is more" trend.
sentences.cn: 1945 至 1962 年间，《加州艺术与建筑》杂志委托才华横溢的现代建筑师设计的“案例研究住宅”，是“少即是多”潮流的又一本土推动力。

sentences.en: Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing.
sentences.cn: 其美学效果来自自然景观、新型材料和直白明快的细部处理。

words.meaning: adj. 直率的，直截了当的

sentences.en: In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.
sentences.cn: 在他的案例研究住宅中，拉尔夫·拉普森或许错误预测了机械革命影响日常生活的方式——几乎没有美国家庭购置直升机，尽管大多数家庭最终用上了烘干机——但他“自给自足既可取又不可避免”的信念得到了广泛认同。

questions.stem: The postwar American housing style largely reflected the Americans' ______.
questions.stem_cn: 战后美国的住宅风格在很大程度上反映了美国人的______。

options.C: restraint and confidence

options_cn.C: 克制与信心
options_cn.D: 自豪与忠诚

questions.explanation: 定位第二段②句：大萧条与战争让美国人学会了节俭度日，“这种克制（restraint），加上战后对未来的信心（confidence），使小而高效的住宅格外时尚”——住宅风格正是这两种心态的反映，C 正确。A 是第一段对战后社会总体特征的描述，并非住宅风格反映的心态；B 是住宅本身的特点而非心态；D 无据。

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from Paragraph 3 about the Bauhaus?
questions.stem_cn: 关于包豪斯，从第三段可以推断出以下哪项？

options.A: It was founded by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.
options.B: Its designing concept was affected by World War II.
options.C: Most American architects used to be associated with it.
options.D: It had a great influence upon American architecture.

options_cn.A: 它由路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗创立
options_cn.B: 它的设计理念受到二战的影响
options_cn.C: 大多数美国建筑师都曾与它有联系
options_cn.D: 它对美国建筑产生了巨大影响

questions.explanation: 定位第三段：①句提到与包豪斯有关的设计师们移居美国、执教建筑院校，②句说“这些设计师对美国建筑的发展进程产生了巨大影响”——These designers 即指与包豪斯相关的人，可推知包豪斯对美国建筑影响巨大，D 正确。A 无据（文中只说密斯与包豪斯有关，未说他创立）；B 无据；C 颠倒（是包豪斯相关人士来到美国，而非多数美国建筑师与它有联系）。

questions.stem: Mies held that elegance of architectural design ______.
questions.stem_cn: 密斯认为建筑设计的优雅______。

options.C: was not reliant on abundant decoration

options_cn.C: 不依赖繁多的装饰
options_cn.D: 与高效无关

questions.explanation: 定位第四段②句：Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance（他认为优雅并非源自繁多），即优雅不依赖大量装饰，C 正确（did not derive from abundance 与 not reliant on abundant decoration 同义）。A、B 与④句“他设计的空间小而高效，而非宽大空旷”相悖；D 与其“小而高效”的理念相反。

questions.stem: What is true about the apartments Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive?
questions.stem_cn: 关于密斯在芝加哥湖滨大道建造的公寓，下列哪项正确？

options.B: They were built with materials popular at that time.
options.C: They were more spacious than neighboring buildings.
options.D: They shared some characteristics of abstract art.

options_cn.A: 它们忽视了细节与比例
options_cn.B: 它们使用当时流行的材料建造
options_cn.C: 它们比邻近建筑更宽敞
options_cn.D: 它们具有抽象艺术的某些特征

questions.explanation: 定位第五段②句末：这些建筑细节与比例的典雅是“当时风行的抽象艺术在建筑上的对应物”，即公寓与抽象艺术有共通特征，D 正确。A 与“细节与比例的典雅”相反；B 曲解——金属、玻璃等材料在 40 年代“象征未来”，并非当时流行；C 与①句“比邻居楼里的公寓更小”相反。

questions.stem: What can we learn about the design of the "Case Study Houses"?
questions.stem_cn: 关于“案例研究住宅”的设计，我们可以知道什么？

options.B: Natural scenes were taken into consideration.
options.C: Details were sacrificed for the overall effect.

options_cn.C: 为整体效果牺牲了细节
options_cn.D: 采用了环保材料

questions.explanation: 定位第七段②句：其美学效果来自自然景观（landscape）、新型材料和直白的细部处理——即设计时考虑并利用了自然景观，B 正确。A 曲解③句（拉普森只是预测机械革命的影响，且预测有误）；C 与“直白明快的细部处理”相悖；D 偷换概念，文中说的是“新型材料”而非环保材料。

articles.title: Will the European Union Make It?
articles.topic: 欧盟向何处去：欧元危机与法德分歧
articles.source: 2011 年考研英语（二）Text 4 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: Will the European Union make it?
sentences.cn: 欧盟能挺过去吗？

sentences.en: The question would have sounded strange not long ago.
sentences.cn: 不久之前，这个问题听起来还会显得奇怪。

sentences.en: Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a "Bermuda triangle" of debt, population decline and lower growth.
sentences.cn: 而现在，就连这一事业最热情的拥护者也在谈论欧洲大陆正面临债务、人口下降和增长放缓构成的“百慕大三角”。

words.meaning: n. 拉拉队员，（喻）鼓吹者、拥护者

sentences.en: As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency.
sentences.cn: 除了那些长期问题之外，欧盟还在其经济核心——使用单一货币的 16 个国家——面临一场急性危机。

sentences.en: Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
sentences.cn: 市场已不再相信：无论强弱，欧元区各经济体有朝一日会凭借共享单一货币的约束而趋于一致——这种约束使缺乏竞争力的成员国无法用货币贬值来快速自救。

words.meaning: 词组：权宜之计，快速解决办法

sentences.en: Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck.
sentences.cn: 然而，关于如何使欧洲单一货币免于解体的讨论陷入了僵局。

words.meaning: adj. 陷入僵局的，卡住的

sentences.en: It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.
sentences.cn: 僵局的原因在于：欧元区的两个主导国家法国和德国，在“欧元区内部需要加强统一”上意见一致，但在“统一什么”上存在分歧。

words.meaning: 词组：主导力量，主导国家

sentences.en: Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey.
sentences.cn: 德国认为，拯救欧元必须依靠在借贷、支出和竞争力方面制定更严格的规则，并对不遵守规则的政府施以准自动的制裁作为后盾。

sentences.en: These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils.
sentences.cn: 这些制裁可能包括威胁冻结欧盟面向较贫困地区和欧盟特大项目的资金，甚至暂停一国在欧盟部长理事会中的投票权。

sentences.en: It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.
sentences.cn: 德国坚持认为，经济协调应涵盖欧盟俱乐部的全部 27 个成员国——在它们当中，支持自由市场主义和从严经济政策的占微弱多数；德国担心，如果只在核心圈内协调，微弱多数将倾向于法国式的干预。

sentences.en: A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members.
sentences.cn: 以法国为首的“南方”阵营则另有所求：在欧元区成员国的核心圈内建立“欧洲经济政府”。

sentences.en: Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers.
sentences.cn: 换句话说，这意味着政治家干预货币政策，并通过共同欧洲债券或彻底的财政转移让各国政府获得更低息的借贷，从而建立一个由较富裕成员国向较贫困成员国再分配的体系。

sentences.en: Finally, figures close to the Franch government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.
sentences.cn: 最后，接近法国政府的人士私下表示，欧元区成员国应就某些财政和社会政策的统一达成共识：例如，抑制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的竞争。

sentences.en: It is too soon to write off the EU.
sentences.cn: 现在就断定欧盟不行还为时过早。

sentences.en: It remains the world's largest trading block.
sentences.cn: 它仍然是世界上最大的贸易集团。

sentences.en: At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area.
sentences.cn: 处于最佳状态时，欧洲一体化事业是非常自由开放的：它建立在由 27 个贫富不一的国家组成的单一市场之上，其内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度远高于任何可比的贸易区。

sentences.en: It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
sentences.cn: 它是一次雄心勃勃的尝试：磨钝全球化最锋利的棱角，让资本主义变得温和良性。

questions.stem: The EU is faced with so many problems that ______.
questions.stem_cn: 欧盟面临如此多的问题，以至于______。

options.A: it has more or less lost faith in markets
options.B: even its supporters begin to feel concerned
options.C: some of its member countries plan to abandon euro
options.D: it intends to deny the possibility of devaluation

options_cn.A: 它已或多或少失去了对市场的信任
options_cn.B: 连它的支持者也开始感到忧虑
options_cn.C: 一些成员国打算放弃欧元
options_cn.D: 它打算否定货币贬值的可能性

questions.explanation: 定位首段③句：“现在连这一事业最热情的拥护者（greatest cheerleaders）也在谈论欧洲大陆面临的‘百慕大三角’”——问题多到连支持者都难以淡定，B 正确（supporters 对应 cheerleaders，feel concerned 对应 talk of）。A 颠倒——是市场对欧元区失去信心；C 无据；D 曲解，原文指单一货币机制使弱国无法靠贬值自救，而非欧盟否定贬值的可能性。

questions.stem: The debate over the EU's single currency is stuck because the dominant powers ______.
questions.stem_cn: 关于欧盟单一货币的讨论陷入僵局，是因为主导国家______。

options.A: are competing for the leading position
options.B: are busy handling their own crises
options.C: fail to reach an agreement on harmonisation
options.D: disagree on the steps towards disintegration

options_cn.C: 未能就统一问题达成一致
options_cn.D: 在瓦解的步骤上存在分歧

questions.explanation: 定位第三段②句：法德两国“同意需要加强欧元区内部统一，但在统一什么上存在分歧（agree on ... but disagree about what to harmonise）”，即未能就统一协调问题达成一致，C 正确。A、B 均属主观臆断；D 拼凑①句 disintegration 与②句 disagree 设障，文中并未谈及“瓦解的步骤”。

questions.stem: To solve the euro problem, Germany proposed that ______.
questions.stem_cn: 为解决欧元问题，德国提议______。

options.A: EU funds for poor regions be increased
options.C: only core members be involved in economic co-ordination
options.D: voting rights of the EU members be guaranteed

options_cn.A: 增加欧盟面向贫困地区的资金
options_cn.C: 只让核心成员国参与经济协调
options_cn.D: 保障欧盟成员国的投票权

questions.explanation: 定位第四段①句：德国认为拯救欧元必须靠“在借贷、支出和竞争力方面更严格的规则”并辅以制裁，B 正确（stricter regulations 对应 stricter rules）。A 与制裁措施“冻结面向贫困地区的欧盟资金”相反；C 与③句“经济协调应涵盖全部 27 个成员国”相反；D 与“暂停一国投票权”的制裁内容相悖。

questions.stem: The French proposal of handling the crisis implies that ______.
questions.stem_cn: 法国应对危机的提议暗示______。

options.A: poor countries are more likely to get funds
options.B: strict monetary policy will be applied to poor countries
options.C: loans will be readily available to rich countries
options.D: rich countries will basically control Eurobonds

options_cn.A: 贫困国家更有可能获得资金
options_cn.B: 将对贫困国家实施严格的货币政策
options_cn.C: 富裕国家将随时能获得贷款
options_cn.D: 欧洲债券基本上将由富裕国家控制

questions.explanation: 定位第五段②句：法国主张的“欧洲经济政府”意味着政治家干预货币政策，并通过低息借贷建立“由较富裕成员国向较贫困成员国再分配”的体系——即倡导贫富国均衡发展，暗示贫困国家更可能获得资金，A 正确。B 相反（严格政策是德国的主张）；C、D 与文意相悖——低息借贷与欧洲债券都是实现向贫困国再分配的途径，受益方是贫困国而非富国。

questions.stem: Regarding the future of the EU, the author seems to feel ______.
questions.stem_cn: 关于欧盟的未来，作者的态度似乎是______。

options.C: conceited

options_cn.C: 自负的
options_cn.D: 有希望的

questions.explanation: 态度题。末段首句“现在就断定欧盟不行还为时过早”定下基调，随后以“仍是世界最大贸易集团”“非常自由开放”“雄心勃勃的尝试”等积极表述肯定欧盟的优势与价值，可见作者对欧盟前景持乐观、抱有希望的态度，D 正确。A、B 均为负面态度，与末段相悖；C 过度引申，作者论述客观，谈不上“自负”。
